title: Gemini Decisions API: 20 Questions, 1 Call, How Sure It Is
description:
Gemini Decisions API explained in 60 seconds: one call with up to 1,000 questions about one input (text, images, audio, video or PDF), and instead of writing text, the gemini-decision-1 model scores the options you gave it (yes/no, multiple choice, rubric), each answer with a confidence from 0 to 1.
Launched November 11, 2026, in the Gemini API in Google AI Studio. Our example: 20 questions about one insurance claim used to mean 20 prompts to a chat model, the claim sent each time; now it's 1 call, the claim billed once (each question still adds its own instruction and criteria tokens).

Read Google's own post first: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/gemini-decisions-api/

Chapters
0:00 20 questions, 1 call
0:15 Our example: claim sent once
0:28 Confidence scores and Google's benchmarks
0:46 What we learned

The story: one counted example. One insurance claim (a scanned PDF and damage photos, the kind of input Google's own post gives as an example) and 20 questions about it. In our example, asking a chat model one question at a time meant 20 prompts, the claim sent each time, 20 essay answers to read, and no number for how sure each one was (a chat model can be asked for one; the one in our example gave none). With the Decisions API, in our example, the claim goes once with all 20 questions: 1 call.

How it works, per Google: you pass one input (text, images, audio, video or PDF, up to 256K tokens) with up to 1,000 independent questions in one request, and the questions can mix yes/no checks, multiple choice and rubric scores. Instead of writing answer text, the gemini-decision-1 model scores the options you give it, so it only chooses among options you defined; it does not write text, summaries or explanations. Every answer includes a confidence score from 0 to 1, so your code can route ambiguous cases to a fallback or a human reviewer (your code does the routing; it is not automatic). A confidence score alone does not establish that an assessment is trustworthy (InfoWorld), so it is not proof an answer is right.

The bill: the shared input is billed once per request no matter how many questions you evaluate, but each question still adds its own instruction and criteria tokens. Google says Gemini Decision 1 with the Decisions API is nearly 5x cheaper across its shared benchmark suite than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite with the Interactions API. That is Google's own comparison on its own benchmarks, not a claim about any other model or any other workload.

Availability: the Gemini Decisions API is available through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio since November 11, 2026. Support in Gemini in Google Cloud is coming soon, per Google.

What we learned: in our example, 20 questions took 20 prompts; now 1 call, each answer with how sure it is.
